local_market_longform:
Columbus is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Columbus currently trade around a median of $285,000 and take roughly 24 days to go under contract, with about 21% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Columbus runs heavily to 1900s–1920s doubles and bungalows near the core, post-war ranches, and newer suburban tracts, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Columbus, the issues we see most are freeze-thaw foundation and basement cracking, aging cast-iron and clay plumbing, knob-and-tube wiring, and older oil-to-gas conversions. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like the Hilltop out to Dublin and Reynoldsburg — and in Ohio the local economy anchored by state government, Ohio State University, insurance and finance, and Intel's new chip plants nearby keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Franklin County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Columbus sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the Ohio Statehouse also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Columbus. We know what a block in the Hilltop, Linden, Franklinton, and Clintonville actually sells for, what central Ohio buyers will and won't pay for, and how Franklin County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Columbus house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Ohio title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Columbus pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Columbus homes in any condition — including the freeze-thaw foundation and basement cracking we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Columbus neighborhood — places like the Hilltop — the home's condition, and current central Ohio demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Ohio?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Ohio (SB 155) requires a bold-faced written disclosure before contract; we provide it and disclose our intent to assign clearly.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Franklin County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
